reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin as an investment opportunity, invites viewers to join through a signup link, and claims guaranteed profits of over 500%. It promotes paid package purchases or upgrades, token increases, rising coin value, large earnings, and recruiting others into a team, while requesting account or contact details.

citations.quote: new investment business opportunity that pays in euros which guarantee of making over 500% profit on your investment
you earn money as the coins rise up to value when the coins rise up in value you make money as well from this one coin business

opening.argument: The material can be read as describing a business and its claimed mechanics, not certifying a risk-free investment. It explains cryptocurrency generally and says that coin value depends on demand and supply. A claim about potential returns, even an extravagant one, is not itself proof that viewers were actually paid or that the creator took their money. The presentation shows claims and an invitation to learn more; the supplied material does not establish that those claims were fulfilled, or that a viewer was compelled to join.

citations.quote: the value of the coin depends on factors such as disability, demand at what what and supply
Both virtual currency and cryptocurrencies are types of digital currencies.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening emphasizes the return claim and package purchases, but a claim is not proof of a completed deceptive transaction. The withdrawal slide describes a process and possible destination accounts; it does not show a failed withdrawal or establish that anyone was unable to access funds. Nor does the signup invitation alone show that the creator concealed terms from viewers.

citations.quote: use this link to sign up

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presenter does not merely discuss variable cryptocurrency prices: he promises guaranteed profits and says packages, token splits, and rising coin value generate earnings. The video explicitly lists payment methods for account upgrades and presents alleged earnings as proof, while inviting viewers to invest. Mentioning demand and supply does not qualify those specific promises or supply evidence that they are reliable.

citations.quote: which guarantee of making over 500% profit on your investment

opening.argument: The presentation has a substantial instructional structure: it defines digital currency and cryptocurrency, compares cryptocurrency with traditional money, and walks through joining, account upgrades, withdrawals, and exchange. Its stated purpose includes explaining how these processes work. The speaker also offers marketing instruction, including video, social-media, email, and blog marketing. That makes this plausibly a tutorial about a business platform and online promotion, even if its claims are optimistic. The materials provided do not independently verify those claims, but neither do they establish that the explanatory content itself is a fraudulent transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats promotional claims as proof of scam, but it does not distinguish an instructional walkthrough from proof of a deceptive outcome. The video does explain cryptocurrency concepts and operational topics, including how to withdraw earnings. A promotional tone or tutorial about joining does not alone establish that the described process failed or that its claims were knowingly false.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format is embedded in a direct investment pitch, not detached education: the speaker invites viewers to invest, describes paid packages and upgrades, and teaches recruitment and marketing to find more investors. The cryptocurrency definitions do not substantiate the promised returns, and operational slides are still part of the solicitation rather than evidence that the investment works as claimed.

citations.quote: I will be showing you how you can make 100% to 500 percent profit on your investment

opening.argument: The video presents a named business with account packages, upgrade options, and stated withdrawal channels. Those are recognizable features of a commercial service, and the material explains that packages can be obtained through several payment methods and that funds may be requested to an account. It also says a viewer can participate without sponsoring anyone. Recruitment commissions are discussed, but the supplied record does not establish that recruiting is mandatory for earnings. Nothing here documents an actual payment, loss, or failed withdrawal, so the evidence supports a promotional business presentation more directly than a completed scam mechanism.

citations.quote: You don't need to sponsor anyone

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's account highlights packages and team commissions, but the video also describes participation without sponsoring anyone and identifies withdrawal methods. A signup link and requests for basic contact details can serve ordinary enrollment and follow-up. The supplied evidence does not show a credential theft, failed withdrawal, or an actual viewer's loss; those cannot be inferred from a presentation alone.

citations.quote: You don't need to sponsor anyone
send me your name username and email

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The ordinary-commerce framing leaves out the central terms: viewers are told to buy or upgrade packages, token balances can multiply through system splits, and income can rise with coin value. The presenter also explains commissions from downline package purchases. These are investment-return and recruitment claims, not just neutral product or service details; no evidence in the video validates the earnings presented.
